tone_statements.citation: Hansson, Inga-Lill. 1989. A comparison of Akha, Hani, Khatu and Pijo. Linguistics of the Tibeto-Burman Area 12(1): 6-91.
tone_statements.quote: Tones: The non-laryngealized High, Mid, and Low tones are written -á, -a, -à; the laryngealized Mid and Low tones are written -aq, -àq. Laryngealization occurs in all finals except -u and -i. (See Appendix 4 for possible syllables.) [...] Aspirated stops and fricatives only occur non-laryngealized. [...] The tonal systems of Khàtú and Píjò correspond exactly to Akha and Hani. The low tone is in all of them slightly falling. Some differences in the tones may depend on sandhi rules, which remain to be worked out for Hani, Khàtú, and Píjò.

tone_statements.citation: Wheatley, Julian K. 1982. Comments on the 'Hani' dialects of Loloish. Linguistics of the Tibeto-Burman Area 7(1): 1-38.
tone_statements.quote: Hu and Dai cite a fair number of examples from Biyue, Kaduo (BI-KA) and Haoni and Baihong (HAO-BAI) varieties, and a small numer from Yani, Jiayin (both HA-YA), Qidi, Meiluo, and Mojiang. Ignoring loanwords from Chinese, we see that all these dialects have the two (phonemic) manners of initial stops characteristic of Hani/Akha, by contrast with the three found in Lahu and Lisu and the four in most Yi. And all show a basic tonal system with three pitch levels, high, mid and low (falling).

tone.says: First-hand phonological system of Khatu (Kaduo): three tones High, Mid, Low on non-laryngealised syllables plus laryngealised Mid and Low (i.e. 5 tone-register categories, no laryngealised High); laryngealisation on all finals except -u and -i; aspirated stops/fricatives only non-laryngealised; the Low tone is slightly falling; tonal system 'corresponds exactly to Akha and Hani'; tone sandhi not yet worked out; proto-Loloish stopped rhymes (laryngealisation) 'on their way out' in Khatu.

sources.note: States that all the Hu & Dai Hani varieties including Kaduo have a basic three-level tone system, high / mid / low(falling) (Lüchun values 55, 33, 31), cross-cut by a tense/lax (laryngealised) register that historically continues proto-Loloish checked syllables; a 35 tone occurs only in Chinese loans (Lüchun). Places Kaduo with Biyue and Haoni at 'stage 6' (voiced stops devoiced, register weakened): in Kaduo four of the eleven vowels (/u̱ u ɪ ɔ/) do not occur in tense syllables (p. 15). Discusses whether pitch, aspiration or vowel quality compensated for register loss (section 3.2). No Kaduo-…
